The minimum uncertainty in energy \(\Delta E\) can be estimated using the Heisenberg uncertainty principle. The uncertainty in position is \(\Delta x = 0.1 \text{ nm} = 1 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}\). The uncertainty in momentum is at least \(\Delta p \approx \frac{\hbar}{2\Delta x}\), where \(\hbar \approx 1.05 \times 10^{-34} \text{ J·s}\).

\[
\Delta p \approx \frac{1.05 \times 10^{-34}}{2 \times 10^{-10}} = 5.25 \times 10^{-25} \text{ kg·m/s}
\]

The electron's speed is \(v = 2 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}\). The uncertainty in energy is related to the uncertainty in momentum by \(\Delta E \approx v \Delta p\) (since \(dE/dp = v\) both relativistically and non-relativistically).

\[
\Delta E \approx (2 \times 10^8) \times (5.25 \times 10^{-25}) = 1.05 \times 10^{-16} \text{ J}
\]

This is approximately \(10^{-16} \text{ J}\).

Answer: D
